readings.subject: Conditional removal of prior SFC approval for material UCITS investment changes, including exceptions and pending applications
readings.statement: For a covered UCITS fund's post-authorisation material change in an investment objective, policy or restriction, prior SFC approval is no longer required under this measure from 2025-11-28 if the change complies with home jurisdiction requirements, involves neither novel nor complex product features, and does not potentially have local policy implications. Covered funds are UCITS domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland or the Netherlands, and UK-domiciled schemes authorised as UK UCITS. If any product-feature or local-policy exception applies, or home requirements are not met, the circular does not remove the otherwise applicable approval requirement. An application received by the SFC before 2025-11-28 and still awaiting approval or authorisation at commencement remains subject to the existing approval or authorisation process; the new relief does not automatically dispose of it. The management company must still address applicable notifications and filings, and the SFC retains post-vetting, enquiry and regulatory-action powers. The actual approval outcome for an excluded or transitional case remains dependent on the existing rules and relevant FAQs, which are not supplied.
readings.distinction: The question answered is whether this circular removes or preserves the otherwise applicable prior-SFC-approval requirement for a material investment change. Relief from prior approval is distinct from home-law compliance, notification, licence possession and overall compliance. For excluded changes, the proposed reading preserves existing approval requirements, subject to the unavailable underlying rules. Formalization is null because the requested complete approval determination depends on those missing rules and the existing application process; encoding only the relief condition would answer a narrower question.

citations.quote: (ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.

assumptions: The specific effective-date and transition provisions govern the general statement that the measures take immediate effect.
The pending-application provision is read as testing whether approval or authorisation remained outstanding at commencement.
An exception to removal preserves an otherwise applicable prior-approval requirement; it does not independently establish every element of that underlying requirement.
No case-specific facts, external FAQ contents or earlier substantive proposal have been supplied.
questions: How do the relevant FAQs distinguish novel or complex product features and changes that may have local policy implications?
Does the existing process require prior approval for the particular excluded or transitional change?

dimensions.explanation: The reading concerns material investment-objective, policy or restriction changes in covered funds after authorisation. It does not decide initial authorisation, operator changes or treatment of funds outside the circular's definition.

Covered funds are UCITS domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland or the Netherlands, and UK-domiciled collective investment schemes authorised as UK UCITS. Materiality, novelty, complexity and potential local policy implications are not defined; their application requires judgment and potentially FAQ or SFC clarification.

Relief requires compliance with home jurisdiction requirements. Novel features, complex features, or possible local policy implications each exclude relief. Pending pre-effective-date applications remain in the existing process.

The SFC removes a prior-approval requirement conditionally. Failure to qualify leaves the existing requirement unaffected; it does not establish a new blanket prohibition. Management companies remain subject to applicable notification and filing obligations, and the SFC retains post-vetting and enforcement powers.

The specific commencement date is 2025-11-28, which gives content to 'immediate effect'. Applications received before that date and awaiting approval or authorisation at commencement continue under the existing process. Receipt on the effective date is not receipt before it. The circular does not explain withdrawal, refiling or modification of pending applications.

A case-specific answer requires home law, the relevant FAQs, forms and checklists, the existing approval process, fund and change characteristics, and application history. External contents and the two packet dependencies missing.1c25ffdf5c1e10e0297748d5 and missing.79fb54125bb1f35a1d457fad are unavailable; their contents are not inferred.

source_packet.selected_slice: Does a material change in a UCITS fund investment objective, policy or restriction require prior SFC approval under this circular, taking account of product features, home requirements and the application transition?

units.text: The Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) regularly reviews its operational processes and guidance to ensure their efficiency without compromising investor interests and protection.

The SFC has further streamlined measures for processing certain post-authorisation matters for UCITS funds1, following its review and engagement with market participants. These measures aim at facilitating UCITS funds in implementing changes that are subject to their home regulator’s supervision, and will take immediate effect.
Further streamlined measures for UCITS funds
The key streamlined measures cover the following post-authorisation matters:
(i)        Change of key operators – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for change of depository and investment delegates which are under the home regulator’s supervision.

(ii)       Material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions – Removing the SFC’s requirement on prior approval for material changes in investment objectives, policies and restrictions which comply with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, except for changes that involve novel or complex product features and/or which may have local policy implications.
(iii)      Post-authorisation notifications – To align the SFC’s notification requirements with the fund’s home jurisdiction requirements, including the notice periods and content requirements.

The SFC has updated and published on its website relevant FAQs2 , including a revamped FAQ on SFC Authorization of UCITS Funds to facilitate UCITS fund managers in navigating post-authorisation compliance matters, as well as related forms and checklists3 .
The streamlined measures set out in the relevant FAQs will take effect on 28 November 2025 (Effective Date).

Existing applications received by the SFC before the Effective Date for which no approval or authorisation has been granted will be processed by the SFC in accordance with the existing approval or authorisation process.

The SFC will continue to conduct post-vetting of scheme changes (including those not subject to the SFC’s prior approval) and related revised documents filed with the SFC. It may make follow-up enquiries and/or take appropriate regulatory actions in case of non-compliance to ensure investor protection.
Should you wish to clarify any aspects of this circular, please contact the relevant case officers in charge.

1 For this circular, UCITS funds means (i) Undertakings for Collective Investment in Transferable Securities (UCITS) domiciled in France, Luxembourg, Ireland and the Netherlands, and (ii) collective investment schemes domiciled in the United Kingdom authorised as UK UCITS.
